name: Definition of Done Workshop
deliverable: Technical consensus alignment on quality gates for release readiness

steps.text: Name the increment the criteria will cover, so the room is agreeing on the same scope.
Ask each person to list what must be true before they would call that increment finished.
Cluster the lists and turn vague items into checks someone could run and mark pass or fail.
Test the draft against a recent release: would these criteria have caught a defect the team shipped?
Agree the final list, including the evidence each check needs, and publish it where work is tracked.
Set a review date and name who may change the definition, so it stays a living standard.

failure: Activity criteria: the list says work was performed, such as code reviewed, but not what must be true, so done still means different things to different people.
intervention: Take each item and ask how a reviewer would verify it in five minutes; if no one can say, rewrite it as a check with evidence.
provenance: Steps written for this deck from the method's public definition; the source has no protocol.

origin.note: A shared team standard from Scrum practice; no single documented originator.
